# What Purix checks and what it does not

<!-- Generated by scripts/generate-checks-page.mjs from docs/claims.json and docs/client-runs.json. Do not edit by hand: change the register and run the script. -->

Generated from the claims register, whose newest entry is dated 2026-11-06. This page describes Release 1: a command-line tool and an MCP server on your own machine. Scope and language details are in [BETA_SCOPE.md](../BETA_SCOPE.md).

## The limits first

Read these before relying on a result. Each sentence is quoted from the register row named after it.

- **Languages.** “…files in languages without a provider are not checked” (COMPL-009) “Purix says so: "Unsupported language, not checked".” (BETA-SCOPE-UNSUPPORTED-LANG)
- **Hooks.** “Those hooks are tested against fake payloads and a real CLI process, and inside one real agent so far” (README-017) “The shell-command check in them is a tripwire, not prevention” (README-034)
- **Isolation.** “Isolation is described here for TypeScript projects on Linux with bubblewrap: it is not checked on macOS (sandbox-exec) or on Python projects, and the test suite uses stand-in tools.” (README-026) “The later re-check of components that depend on the changed one runs with your project folder writable, not in the copy” (README-027)
- **Confidence cutoff.** “The threshold is 0.75 on the model's own stated confidence; nothing here measures how often a change above it is wrong, so Purix states no safety rate for it” (README-028)
- **Secrets.** “The scanner recognises only some secret formats, so a secret in an unknown format, or one that is split or encoded, is sent as it is.” (README-032)
- **Dependency scan.** “During verification, a change that adds a dependency is looked up for known vulnerabilities and for whether the package exists only when `PURIX_DEP_LOOKUP` is set (see the next bullets); it is off by default, so by default those dependencies are listed as "not checked".” (COMPL-004) “It reads the report of pnpm 10 and 11, Yarn 1 and 4, and npm 10, and prints "skipped" instead of "no known vulnerabilities" when the package manager gives anything that is not an audit report, for example when the registry cannot be reached.” (README-033)
- **Tests.** “A passing test run is not proof that the code is correct.” (README-025)

Windows, macOS and Cursor are experimental. Results are reported, not settled: the register has no status that means a second person has re-run a result, so none of it is called settled.

  - Note: A4-1 minimal. The TypeScript compiler step is not yet isolated, so strict mode refuses TypeScript checks on every machine until tsc is routed through the isolated runner (slice T1).

  - Note: A7-1 extension. Known formats only; synthetic tokens built here, not the review's original probe set. Encoded or split secrets are still not detected.

## Checked only in simulation

These have been exercised with simulated agents or payloads, or in one run by the person who made the change. They are the first candidates for a re-run by someone else.

- “`purix hooks install` adds agent hooks that block direct edits to governed files for Claude Code,” (README-016; README). Evidence: `scripts/ci-bypass-flow.mjs`, `scripts/ci-hook-flow.mjs`.
  - Note: Simulated agents only: the installed commands are run by a script, not by the agent. docs/client-runs.json holds one OpenCode run (Windows); no other agent has been run.
- “It reads the report of pnpm 10 and 11, Yarn 1 and 4, and npm 10, and prints "skipped" instead of "no known vulnerabilities" when the package manager gives anything that is not an audit report, for example when the registry cannot be reached.” (README-033; README). Evidence: `packages/core/src/security/deps_audit.real_output.test.ts`, `packages/core/src/security/fixtures/audit/pnpm10_vulnerable.meta.json`.
  - Note: Simulated: fake pnpm, yarn and npm executables replay the real stdout and exit code recorded on 2026-11-07 (see fixtures/audit/*.meta.json for versions). Linux only. Not run: Yarn 2 and 3, Windows, macOS, a real timeout of each tool, HTTP 410 from the registry. Before the fix this row was a stated limit (pnpm 10/11 read as 0 findings).
- “The shell screen misses most ways to write a file it was meant to catch.” (F09-01; research: PURIX-RESEARCH-09-INTERCEPTION-ENFORCEMENT-AND-HOST-AGENTS). Evidence: `packages/core/src/hooks/decide_whole_command.test.ts`.
  - Since then: A9-1: whole-command scan. Probe p1 after: 4 of 41 pass (script file x2, npm run, base64 to sh: design limits, kept as tests), 0 false blocks. Real decision function, Linux, synthetic project; no agent run. Wording stays "tripwire".
- “2 misses are tool names” (F09-02; research: PURIX-RESEARCH-09-INTERCEPTION-ENFORCEMENT-AND-HOST-AGENTS). Evidence: `packages/core/src/hooks/decide_whole_command.test.ts`.
  - Since then: A9-1: classified by input shape (path key = write, shell key = shell); read-looking names and Purix MCP tools exempt.
- “MCP diff ingest applied no Deterministic Override Floor and logged no gate decision.” (F09-05; docs/HOOKS). Evidence: `packages/mcp-server/src/trustgate_floor_wiring.test.ts`.
  - Since then: A9-1: one shared helper applyDeterministicFloor used on the MCP instruction and diff paths, with the decision recorded. Source-level guard plus helper unit tests; no end-to-end MCP ingest run.
- “A cloned repository could supply Purix's tool records and tool binaries from its own .purix/tools folder, and a record's binary path could point outside its tool folder.” (F-T1-01; docs/EVIDENCE). Evidence: `packages/core/src/tools/t1_project_is_data.test.ts`.
  - Since then: Tool state moved to the user's folder, keyed per project; unsafe binary paths refused; an in-project tools folder is reported as ignored. Limit: the project's own node_modules tools (tsc, eslint, test runner) are still used first by design and run isolated, so the claim is only that Purix's own tools are not taken from the project. Linux only.
- “The notification webhook was signed with a literal default secret when none was configured, so anyone could forge the signature.” (F-WH-01; docs/EVIDENCE). Evidence: `packages/core/src/cli-io/notify.test.ts`.
  - Since then: With no secret set, nothing is sent and a warning is printed. Limit: the secret is still a shared key held by Purix and the receiver; this does not authenticate the receiver.
- “A diff hunk that is not at its stated line is applied only where its old side matches in exactly one place in the whole file; there is no fixed distance limit.” (F-ING-01; docs/EVIDENCE). Evidence: `packages/core/src/entrypoints/ingest_shifted_hunks.test.ts`, `scripts/replay-ingest-corpus.mts`.
  - Since then: Probes at shifts 0, 1, 3, 10 and 300, a block duplicated nearby and far away (refused), a block absent (refused). Replay on real history, 2026-11-06: the last 150 commits of express, click and execa (shallow clones), every modified text file, hunk headers shifted by 0, 1, 3, 10, 60 and 300 lines: 1,933 files, 0 applied wrongly. At shift 0 all applied; at each shifted size 4 were refused (a one-line .npmrc under the minimum-anchor rule, and three test files with repeated lines, so no unique match). 157 added files were byte-identical. Limit: 150 commits per repo from shallow clones, not the 450-commit corpus; one author's run, not re-run by a second person; the 1,018-file rerun against compile.ts is still undone.
- “A blank context line whose leading space was stripped is read as a blank context line while the hunk header still expects lines, and a diff cut off in the middle of a hunk is refused instead of applied as a shorter hunk.” (F-ING-02; docs/EVIDENCE). Evidence: `packages/core/src/entrypoints/ingest_anchor_rules.test.ts`.
  - Since then: Seven probes (blank rescue, cut-off last hunk refused, a miscount in the middle recounted, complete diff unaffected, 1-line anchor refused, all-blank anchor refused, 3-line anchor moves). Limit: a last hunk whose header over-counts is refused (it cannot be told from a cut-off); the share of real diffs this affects is unmeasured because the replay corpus was not rebuilt.
- “A custom model-provider block that arrives with a project is refused and nothing is sent until the person accepts it, and an accepted endpoint is not accepted for a different key variable or address.” (F-1015-01; docs/EVIDENCE). Evidence: `packages/core/src/llm/providers_custom_trust.test.ts`.
  - Since then: Limit: covers the provider block only, not what a model returns.
- “The verification copy leaves out .env and .git, and secrets, config and the manifest.” (F-1015-02; docs/EVIDENCE). Evidence: `packages/core/src/sandbox/sandbox_copy_scope.test.ts`.
  - Since then: Limit: a copy-scope rule; a file the project's own tests read from outside the copy is not covered.
- “A corrupt state file, such as a provider config, is set aside as a copy before it is replaced, and the quarantine step never throws for a missing file.” (F-1015-03; docs/EVIDENCE). Evidence: `packages/core/src/platform/atomic_write.test.ts`.
  - Since then: Limit: keeps the evidence of what was there; it does not repair the file.
- “Each audit append writes a receipt holding the newest head hash.” (F-1015-04; docs/EVIDENCE). Evidence: `packages/core/src/security/audit_receipt.test.ts`.
  - Since then: Limit: someone who can rewrite the receipt and the chain together is not caught; a chain with no receipt is not flagged.
- “Tools that Purix runs through its sandbox run with the project read-only and the network off, with one scratch folder writable that is not the project.” (F-1015-05; docs/EVIDENCE). Evidence: `packages/core/src/sandbox/tool_run.test.ts`.
  - Since then: Limit: checked on Linux only (the test is Linux-gated); Windows and macOS isolation is a separate, unverified claim.
- “A project's dof-patterns.json adds to the built-in protected paths and never replaces them, and an empty list is refused and the built-in paths are used.” (F-DOF-01; docs/EVIDENCE). Evidence: `packages/core/src/gates/trustgate.test.ts`.
  - Since then: Limit: decides which files always need a person; a file not registered to a component is not covered.
- “An unquoted password in an env-file or shell style line, such as DB_PASSWORD=value or export PGPASSWORD=value, is redacted before text goes to a model provider when the value mixes letters and digits.” (F-SCR-01; docs/EVIDENCE). Evidence: `packages/core/src/security/outbound_scrub.test.ts`.
  - Since then: Probe on 16 common token formats: 14 caught with generated values, JWT and generic key assignment caught with realistic values, unquoted password was the one real miss and is now caught. Limit: letters-only or digits-only passwords are not caught; formats the list does not know still go out.
- “A diff may delete files of the component it is ingested against: the deleted file is removed from the verification copy, the writer re-checks that it still holds what was verified before removing it, the journal marks it deleted so a crash can be recovered either way, and the change always needs a person's confirmation.” (F-DEL-01; docs/EVIDENCE). Evidence: `packages/core/src/entrypoints/ingest_deletions.test.ts`, `packages/core/src/sandbox/sandbox_remove_paths.test.ts`, `packages/core/src/entrypoints/modify_writer_delete.test.ts`, `packages/core/src/state/reconcile_deletion.test.ts`, `packages/core/src/manifest/commit_and_cascade_deletion.test.ts`.
  - Since then: Before: a diff that deleted a file was parsed and then refused. Now: tracked, non-test files may be deleted while others remain; deleting a test file, an untracked file or the last file is refused; a failing change that deletes files is not sent to automatic repair; the dependents check always runs. Limits: tested with stand-in language providers and a real store, not yet with a real agent or a real TypeScript compiler; the CLI path is typechecked and shares the helper but has no end-to-end test of its own; a deleted file's now-empty folder is left in place.
- “…purix check fails when the audit head receipt is ahead of the audit chain, and an emptied chain with governed components is no longer reported as nothing to verify.” (F-AUD-02; docs/EVIDENCE). Evidence: `packages/core/src/entrypoints/check.test.ts`.
  - Since then: Limit: someone who can edit the store and the receipt together removes records unseen; the git anchor is the second line. With no receipt a wiped chain cannot be told from a fresh one, and the check says so.
- “PURIX_MCP_AUTO_APPROVE=1 is ignored while PURIX_STRICT_ISOLATION is on: the normal prompt or pending approval runs and the refusal is recorded.” (F-MCP-02; docs/EVIDENCE). Evidence: `packages/mcp-server/src/mcp_approval_and_paths.test.ts`.
  - Since then: Limit: the rule follows PURIX_STRICT_ISOLATION only; if a different setting was meant, it is one call to change.
- “A hunk is moved away from the line its header gives only when its old side has at least three non-blank lines, or sits flush against the start or end of the file.” (F-ING-03; docs/EVIDENCE). Evidence: `packages/core/src/entrypoints/ingest_shifted_hunks.test.ts`.
  - Since then: Limit: three is not a measured number; the 1,018-file replay corpus was not uploaded, so the share of real diffs affected is unknown.

## Limits Purix states about itself

Each of these is something Purix does not do, or does only in part.

- “Those hooks are tested against fake payloads and a real CLI process, and inside one real agent so far” (README-017; README). Evidence: `docs/client-runs.json`.
  - Note: This sentence is true only while docs/client-runs.json holds exactly one passing row (OpenCode, win32-x64, 2026-11-03); update it when another real run is recorded.
- “There is no local license key. Until the entitlement signing key ships in the client, the cached answer is not signature-checked, so someone who edits that cache file can change what their own copy of the client allows.” (README-024; README). Evidence: `packages/core/src/licensing/entitlement_signature.ts`.
  - Note: True only until C-43 ships the key. When it does, this sentence must change and a test that a hand-edited cache is refused with the key present (tier_signed.test.ts has one for a configured key) becomes the evidence.
- “A passing test run is not proof that the code is correct.” (README-025; README)
  - Note: A disclaimer, not a capability.
- “Isolation is described here for TypeScript projects on Linux with bubblewrap: it is not checked on macOS (sandbox-exec) or on Python projects, and the test suite uses stand-in tools.” (README-026; README). Evidence: `packages/core/src/sandbox/sandbox_exec_platform.test.ts`.
  - Note: A limit, true until a real-machine run on macOS and on Python is on file (plan A10e).
- “The later re-check of components that depend on the changed one runs with your project folder writable, not in the copy” (README-027; README). Evidence: `packages/core/src/verify/tests.ts`.
  - Note: Read in code (verify/impact.ts calls provider.runTests with the real targetDir; verify/tests.ts passes writableDir: baseDir). Not asserted by a test.
- “The threshold is 0.75 on the model's own stated confidence; nothing here measures how often a change above it is wrong, so Purix states no safety rate for it” (README-028; README). Evidence: `packages/core/src/gates/trustgate.ts`.
  - Note: Wording rule from the plan (D12). Changes only if a golden set measuring the scorer exists.
- “The scanner recognises only some secret formats, so a secret in an unknown format, or one that is split or encoded, is sent as it is.” (README-032; README). Evidence: `packages/core/src/security/secrets.ts`.
  - Note: A7-1: on a reconstructed probe set (research 03's folder was never uploaded) the write scanner now catches 19 of 22 synthetic tokens and the outbound scrub removes 22 of 22; 0 of 13 ordinary strings flagged. The 3 scan misses (hex under a key name, URL password, short quoted password) are scrub-only by design. Research 03 measured 9 of 22 on its own set, so the two numbers are not directly comparable.
- “The shell-command check in them is a tripwire, not prevention” (README-034; README). Evidence: `docs/HOOKS.md`.
  - Note: Wording rule from the plan (D02).
- “No safety rate is stated for the `0.75` cutoff” (COMPL-001; docs/compliance/eu-ai-act/technical-documentation). Evidence: `packages/core/src/gates/trustgate.ts`.
  - Note: Same rule as README-028.
- “During verification, a change that adds a dependency is looked up for known vulnerabilities and for whether the package exists only when `PURIX_DEP_LOOKUP` is set (see the next bullets); it is off by default, so by default those dependencies are listed as "not checked".” (COMPL-004; docs/compliance/data-and-dependency-governance). Evidence: `packages/cli/src/cli/commands/observability.ts`.
  - Note: Research 03 findings 2 and 3; runVulnScan is called only by audit and the conformance runner. Reworded 2026-11-12 (H-round): the opt-in lookup (PURIX_DEP_LOOKUP, D-q) now exists, so the limit is stated as off by default rather than absent.
- “A name is the operating-system user name, not a cryptographic identity” (COMPL-006; docs/compliance/eu-ai-act/human-oversight). Evidence: `packages/core/src/security/auth.ts`.
  - Note: Risk R-03.
- “It is an ordinary table and is not hash-chained.” (COMPL-007; docs/compliance/eu-ai-act/logging-and-recordkeeping). Evidence: `packages/core/src/manifest/events.ts`.
- “The Team-tier fields `rbac` and `sharedRepoMemory` were removed from `tier.ts` on 2026-10-14” (COMPL-008; docs/compliance/iso-42001/risk-assessment-register). Evidence: `packages/core/src/licensing/tier.ts`.
- “…files in languages without a provider are not checked” (COMPL-009; docs/compliance/eu-ai-act/technical-documentation). Evidence: `BETA_SCOPE.md`.
  - Note: Plan blocker 4: the result does not yet say 'not checked' in every case (A10a-1).

## Research findings: what is still open

These came from the research documents in `docs/research/`. Each says how the fact was obtained (read the code, ran it, or both) and by whom. Where a fix has landed, the last column says what changed. Rows that say Re-checked were read again against the current code by sessions that did not write the finding, and the named tests were run on Linux with a stubbed model; that is not a real-agent, Windows or macOS run, so no row is called settled.

## What this page does not cover

Purix is not certified against ISO/IEC 42001 or the EU AI Act, and nothing here claims it is. The compliance documents in `docs/compliance/` describe what the code does today and list known gaps. A test that passes shows what Purix's checks reported on one machine and nothing more.
